sources.title: Edgar Thurston and K. Rangachari, Castes and Tribes of Southern India, volume 1 (Government Press, Madras, 1909), Badhōyi
sources.locator: Selected printed125–128, scan225–228; title scan7. Full entry begins printed124, not visually inspected this turn.
sources.status: Historical transcription reused and facsimile title/printed125–128 actually collated this turn.
findings: Reports council officers and a fund using larger fines for poorer members’ marriage costs and council expenses.
Describes rent-free land tied to village festival-car construction, agricultural implements and officials’ tent-pegs.
Calls Maharana a title and reports Bindhani Rathno/Bindham Bushano as zamindar-conferred craft distinctions.
Derivation from vardhaki is expressly reported, not established formation history.
D. Mahanty’s wedding description is explicitly shared with other Ganjam castes.
limits: Colonial classifications, hierarchy and gender prejudice are not present-day facts. Do not universalise reported intermarriage or infer identical modern identities.
No dated founding event established; historical title is not proof every Bindhani is equivalent.
